chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Wilbur De Paris, Vic Dickinson, Floyd Brady and J. C. Higginbotham
summary: Jackson recalls Wilbur De Paris, Vic Dickinson of Xenia, Stump Brady who taught him and whose place he took with Zack White, and Higginbotham.

bands.name: Andy Kirk's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And, of course, Wilbur DeParis to me was a good trombone player, a very good trombone player. He was a what you call all-around trombone player. Vic Dickinson. Vic Dickinson left home before I did.
Oh, yes, down there where Wilberforce University is. Yeah, he's from Xenia.

Then there was a little trombone player named Stump Brady, Floyd Brady. Floyd Brady, I took his place with Zack Whyte's band, and when I first left home when I went to Cincinnati he was the first person to ever give me any kind of a lesson and let me practice with him. He was a very little guy.
He's still around. He doesn't play
But he left Zack Whyte and went to Andy Kirk and the 12 Clouds of Joy, and that's how I got in Zack Whyte's band.
: I used to hear Keg Johnson always mentioned him and how much he admired him.
Oh, yes. Well, Stump, you know, Stump played with them a long time, with Andy Kirk. Then he came to New York, of course, with Teddy Wilson and that beautiful band.
: Well, we've got Big Green. What about J. C. Higgenbotham?
J. C. Higgenbotham, when I first heard him, he was another one. He used to play a lot of execution and all at once he changed and went to playing a lot of blues, you know.
